purpose: Generate disposable research work for Forge. Production files and the ten production specialists are protected.

questions: Compare prompt wording that asks for a minimal materialised edit versus an explicit verification-first edit.
Test whether fresh source context versus concise source context changes materialisation reliability.
Test whether asking the agent to state acceptance criteria before editing improves verified output.
Compare diff, udiff, whole-file and scoped editing for preserving exports.
Test symbol-first targeting versus file-level targeting on a small safe change.
Test planning-first versus direct-edit protocol and measure overhead versus materialisation.
Replay stale-anchor recovery and classify controller, model, materialisation and scope failure separately.
Test one bounded recovery retry with changed context and compare it with immediate deterministic fallback.
Test recovery after a deliberately rejected candidate without touching protected production files.
Measure local validation, model invocation and materialisation overhead separately.
Compare fast and deep context budgets for the same benchmark.
Compare Node subprocess, Python subprocess and direct Ollama HTTP control paths.
Test resistance to unrelated instructions while preserving the requested edit.
Generate adversarial cases for stale anchors, export deletion and scope escape.
Fuzz Planner to Builder and Builder to QA contract boundaries with explicit expected receipts.
Design and test a retry controller that preserves candidate identity and evidence.
Compare queue, dispatch and fan-in orchestration patterns for worker isolation.
Test a handoff protocol containing base SHA, candidate SHA, QA receipt and reviewer receipt.
Compare model-only planning with workspace editing and classify where failures occur.
Probe OpenHands SDK availability and separate adapter failure from model failure.
Define a fair benchmark for comparing local coding adapters under equal timeout and context budgets.
Propose a new disposable worker type from observed failure classes and define its benchmark.
Generate alternative worker-controller programs and select one falsifiable experiment.
Design a durable experiment memory record and test whether it improves retest selection.
Test rolling worker replacement when a research job finishes early.
Design a safe research control plane that can discover and benchmark future worker bots.
Test whether a central completed-work inbox improves experiment reuse and retirement decisions.
Replay a known production failure using an isolated fixture and verify classification.
Retest a previously promising idea with one changed meaningful variable.
Compare deterministic control evidence against an LLM path under identical acceptance checks.
